Clean bibliometric keywords

Source: R/keywords_clean.R
keywords_clean.Rd

Gives each concept one spelling in the author keywords (bibliometrix's `DE`) and returns the data frame, ready for bibliometrix. Only papers whose keywords change are rewritten; the others keep their text exactly. Nothing is ever deleted.

The confirmed steps, applied with no review: 1. **Cleanup**: HTML entities decoded, dashes and quotes unified, `&` written `AND`, a leading `#` and trailing punctuation dropped, spacing squeezed, upper case. A keyword cleanup would leave empty (`.`) keeps its written form. 2. **Brackets**: a plural marker goes (`VOICE ASSISTANT(S)`); an acronym in brackets goes (`NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING (NLP)`, also `B-RNN (BI-DIRECTIONAL ...)`); other brackets lose only the brackets. 3. **Your tables**: the `OLD` to `NEW` rows of `replace`; chains (`A` to `B`, `B` to `C`) resolve to the last term, and a later row overrides an earlier one that contradicts it. 4. **Same keyword, written differently**: forms that differ only by case, punctuation, accents, spaces, hyphens or plural (`CHAT BOT`, `CHAT-BOT`, `CHATBOTS`) become one, in word order (`TEXT TO SPEECH` and `SPEECH TO TEXT` stay apart): a `NEW` term of `replace` if one is among them, else the form in most papers. 5. Each keyword once per paper.

`level = "all"` merges nothing: it returns `data` unchanged and writes every merge to the `decisions` sheet, for a person, a model or a tool such as OpenRefine to check outside R, with a short prompt for a model beside it. The sheet has one group per `name` (the keyword the group becomes): its `confirmed` merges (the steps above) and its `needs_revision` candidates, found in six ways (`source`), none by comparing all pairs: * `spelling`: character trigrams, Jaccard 0.7 or more, by MinHash; * `word order`: the same words in another order (`PSYCHOLOGY, CLINICAL`); * `ngram`: the same letter pairs (OpenRefine's 2-gram fingerprint); * `stem`: the words share their stems (Porter; needs SnowballC); * `acronym`: an acronym whose long form is written in brackets elsewhere in the data; * `initials`: an acronym spelled by the initials of a keyword (`NLP`, `NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING`).

Most of these propose some wrong pairs (`APPLICATION` / `APPLICABILITY` share a stem), which is why candidates wait for a `yes`. Spelled alike is not the same concept (`JUSTICE` / `INJUSTICE`). Only keywords in at least `min_papers` papers go to the sheet, each of them, grouped or alone (`single`), so a tool such as OpenRefine can also cluster the whole list itself. Bring the checked sheet back with [keywords_merge()]: by its `merge` answers, or by the edits of `keyword` against the untouched `keyword_backup`.

Usage

keywords_clean(
  data,
  columns = "DE",
  level = c("confirmed", "all"),
  decisions = NULL,
  min_papers = 5,
  replace = NULL,
  titles = "TI",
  output = c("minimal", "all")
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per paper, such as a bibliometrix data frame. The cleaners chain: `M |> authors_clean(ids = "scopus_exports") |> keywords_clean()`.

columns

Names of the keyword columns, `;`-separated. Default `"DE"` (author keywords).

level

`"confirmed"` (default) or `"all"`; see above.

decisions

With `level = "all"`: the sheet to write, a new path ending in `.xlsx` or `.csv` (an existing file is never replaced). Its columns: `group`, `name`, `keyword`, `keyword_backup` (a copy of `keyword` that [keywords_merge()] matches on, so an edit of `keyword` does no harm), `status` (`single` for a keyword in no group, `confirmed` or `needs_revision`), `papers`, `source` (`same spelling`, `your table`, or the ways a candidate was found, see above) and `example` (the title of a paper using the keyword). The prompt goes to `<sheet>_prompt.txt` and, in an `.xlsx`, to a second tab `prompt`.

min_papers

Only keywords in at least this many papers go into the sheet. Default 5: on a 2-million-paper psychology corpus, the 10% of author keywords in 5 or more papers carry 81% of all keyword uses.

replace

Your replacement table: a data frame with columns `OLD` and `NEW` (more columns are ignored), or the path to a `.csv`, `.xlsx` or `.xls` file holding one. An [ask_ai()] result or a [review_sheet()] file also works (its accepted pairs are applied). Several tables are applied in order, so a later table corrects an earlier one. Reading `.xlsx`/`.xls` needs readxl.

titles

Name of the title column, used for the `example` column of the sheet. Default `"TI"`; skipped when `data` has no such column.

output

`"minimal"` (default) returns `data` with the keyword columns rewritten and nothing added. `"all"` also adds `<column>_ORIGINAL` for each column, as it came in (kept when `data` already has it).

Value

With `level = "confirmed"`: `data`, same class, rows and columns, with the keyword columns rewritten where they change (`"; "`-separated); with `output = "all"`, plus the `_ORIGINAL` columns. With `level = "all"`: `data` unchanged (the sheet is the result). A message reports, per column, the written forms that became one keyword and the papers changed.

Errors

Raises `saqrmisc_bad_input` for a missing or non-character keyword column, a `replace` table without `OLD` and `NEW` or a `replace` file that does not exist or is not `.csv`/`.xlsx`/`.xls`, `decisions` given with `level = "confirmed"`, missing or already existing with `"all"`, and a `min_papers` that is not one positive number; `saqrmisc_missing_package` for `.xlsx` without readxl / writexl. Warns `saqrmisc_replace_conflict`, listing each row, when `replace` has rows overridden by a later row.

References

Broder, A. Z. (1997). On the resemblance and containment of documents. *Proceedings of Compression and Complexity of Sequences*, 21-29. doi:10.1109/SEQUEN.1997.666900

Porter, M. F. (1980). An algorithm for suffix stripping. *Program*, 14(3), 130-137. \doi10.1108/eb046814

Leskovec, J., Rajaraman, A., & Ullman, J. D. (2020). *Mining of Massive Datasets* (3rd ed.), chapter 3. Cambridge University Press.

See also

[keywords_merge()] to bring the checked sheet back.

Examples

papers <- data.frame(
  TI = c("Paper one", "Paper two", "Paper three"),
  DE = c("CHATBOT; NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING (NLP); AI",
         "CHAT-BOTS; NLP; ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE",
         "CHATBOTS; E-LEARNING; SURVEY")
)
keywords_clean(papers)
#> keywords: DE: 9 written forms became 7 keywords; 3 papers changed
#>            TI                                       DE
#> 1   Paper one CHATBOT; NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING; AI
#> 2   Paper two    CHATBOT; NLP; ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
#> 3 Paper three              CHATBOT; E-LEARNING; SURVEY
keywords_clean(papers, replace = data.frame(OLD = "AI", NEW = "ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE"),
               output = "all")
#> keywords: DE: 9 written forms became 6 keywords; 3 papers changed
#>            TI                                                            DE
#> 1   Paper one CHATBOT; NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING; ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
#> 2   Paper two                         CHATBOT; NLP; ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
#> 3 Paper three                                   CHATBOT; E-LEARNING; SURVEY
#>                                      DE_ORIGINAL
#> 1 CHATBOT; NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING (NLP); AI
#> 2        CHAT-BOTS; NLP; ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
#> 3                   CHATBOTS; E-LEARNING; SURVEY

# Every merge to a sheet, for a person or a model to check.
sheet <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
cleaned <- keywords_clean(papers, level = "all", decisions = sheet, min_papers = 1)
#> file1e5139b2d1e7.csv: 5 groups and single keywords, 2 confirmed merges and 2 to check, keywords in 1 or more papers. Nothing is merged yet: add a column `merge` (yes or no), then keywords_merge(data, decisions = "file1e5139b2d1e7.csv"). A prompt for a model is in file1e5139b2d1e7_prompt.txt.
utils::read.csv(sheet)
#>   group                        name    keyword keyword_backup         status
#> 1     1                     CHATBOT  CHAT-BOTS      CHAT-BOTS      confirmed
#> 2     1                     CHATBOT   CHATBOTS       CHATBOTS      confirmed
#> 3     2     ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE         AI             AI needs_revision
#> 4     3                  E-LEARNING E-LEARNING     E-LEARNING         single
#> 5     4 NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING        NLP            NLP needs_revision
#> 6     5                      SURVEY     SURVEY         SURVEY         single
#>   papers        source     example
#> 1      1 same spelling            
#> 2      1 same spelling            
#> 3      1      initials   Paper one
#> 4      1               Paper three
#> 5      1       acronym   Paper two
#> 6      1               Paper three
